description:
Join our hardware team as AI Accelerator Design verification engineer verifying the state of the art AI chip, with hands-on ownership of verification environments from test plan through coverage closure and  SI bring-up.
 

What you'll do

 Develop verification plans for AI accelerator blocks: tensor processing, fabric / network-on-chip, and SoC flows

 Write and debug SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches, checkers, stimulus, scoreboards, and reference models for your assigned block or subsystem

 Build emulation-friendly testbenches: synthesizable, transactor-based environments that run the same tests in simulation and on emulators or FPGA prototypes

 Use agentic AI tools across the verification workflow: generating test plans from specifications, writing and reviewing testbench code, triaging regression failures, root-causing bugs, and analyzing coverage. Review and validate everything the agents produce.

 Verify numerical correctness of compute datapaths (FP*) against bit-accurate golden models

 Run real ML kernels and random programs on the RTL, co-simulated against an ISA/architectural reference model

 Define, implement, and close functional and code coverage goals, analyzing holes and driving them to closure

 Debug failures across RTL, testbench, and reference models, and work with RTL designers to root-cause and resolve bugs

 Apply formal verification, assertions (SVA), and emulation where appropriate to improve verification quality and efficiency

 Run and maintain regressions across simulation, emulation, and FPGA platforms, and track bug trends and verification progress metrics

 Partner with RTL design, performance modeling, CAD/methodology, and software teams to align on verification strategy, improve tools and flows, and drive shared quality, schedule, and tape-out goals

 Participate in microarchitecture, RTL, and verification reviews, and write technical documentation


What we're looking for

 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.

 Strong foundation in AI accelerator and computer architecture and digital design, with solid understanding of following:


 Tensor cores and SIMT / SIMD / vector processing

 Floating-point / computer arithmetic, including reduced-precision formats

 On-chip memories, scratchpads, and DMA engines

 Cache hierarchy, memory systems, and HBM/DRAM interfaces

 Network-on-chip and on-chip interconnects

 Dataflow, scheduling, and synchronization across many compute cores



 Working knowledge of modern AI accelerator flows and ISAs, including familiarity with ISA simulators or reference models

 Proficiency in System Verilog, C/C++, assembly

 Familiarity with emulation-friendly verification (synthesizable testbenches, transactors) is a plus

 Hands-on experience using agentic AI tools across the engineering workflow: delegating multi-step tasks to agents, writing clear instructions and context, and checking their results critically

 Scripting experience for automation, test generation, regression management, or data analysis, such as Python, Tcl, or Rust

 Exposure to ML frameworks or workloads (PyTorch, TensorFlow, or ONNX) is a plus
